about: nxsuite inventory: the 147 hardware claims (spec v1) and the test table that answers them. Read by tools/hwtests/nxsuite_gen.py (the .nex test table) and tools/hwtests/intake.py. GPL-3.0-or-later, part of nexclash.

platforms.about: The machine list of the first-start questionnaire (gq.asm, model=): a two-key code and a name of at most 26 characters, shown in this order (at most 17). Adding a platform is a change here only: nxsuite_gen.py puts the list in the string page and checks it. What the operator says is a claim about the machine, not a measurement; the intake shows it beside the measured identity. The names come from the owner's platform summary, not from a register source. ZXnano / MSXnano / A800nano are not Next cores: the suite cannot run there.

list.measured: identifies as machine $0A / board $00 (NextReg $00 / $0F, nxsuite on core 3.03.00, 2026-11-24), the same as an official Issue 2: the registers cannot tell them apart

planned_groups.about: Reserved, NOT built: ids, menu keys and stage for peripheral groups. Each is left out as 'planned: needs hardware the first board lacks / a write-capable probe design'. Only reads a cited source documents as safe may ever be built without a hazard screen; anything that transmits, joins a network, or writes an RTC or flash is opt-in with its own hazard screen; WiFi credentials are never stored or printed. nxsuite_gen.py does not read this list (no menu row, no table entry).
planned_groups.room: Menu: NGROUPS = 14 fills rows 3-16; NEXT STEP is at rows 18-20 and the key lines at 22-23, so three more groups need the group list in two columns (or the NEXT STEP text moved up a row each). Bank 0 (harness + test table) has about 20 bytes left: three gtab entries (8 bytes each) and their test-table rows (12 bytes a test) do not fit without moving code out of bank 0. Overlay room (2026-11-24): page 40 $EDD8-$EFFF (~550 bytes), page 42 $F6EC-$F7FF (~270), page 43 after G5 / G8 / V up to G5PAL, page 61 $FEAA-$FFFF (~340), page 63 $FFAC- (~80), page 41 $F7AB-$F7FF (~80), string page 62 ~200 bytes after the questionnaire; each group needs its own overlay page of code, so a new page would have to come from the suite's 32-63 range by giving up one of the Layer 2 pages 44-53 (V tests draw 320 x 256 there).

tests.title: printer buffer after NEXLOAD
tests.purpose: Does NEXLOAD change the 48K printer buffer ($5B00-$5BFF) after it has loaded bank 5 of a .nex, and which bytes?
tests.method: The .nex image fills $5B00-$5BFF with a known pattern (byte i = i*7+$11). The very first thing the program does after setting its stack is compare those 256 bytes with the pattern: it counts the bytes that differ and notes the offset of the first and last changed byte. Nothing is written. Result in bytes.
tests.expect: docs/BRIEFING.md:391 and :435, lesson.nexload-printer-buffer: NEXLOAD overwrites the whole printer buffer $5B00-$5BFF (NextZXOS paging routines and system variables) after loading bank 5. Claim text: NextZXOS 2.10 wrote only $5B00-$5B65.
tests.needs: The .nex started by NEXLOAD from NextZXOS (the result is the state NEXLOAD leaves).
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: S00: v = number of bytes in $5B00-$5BFF that differ from the loaded pattern (bytes); first = offset ($hh) of the first changed byte; last = offset ($hh) of the last changed byte (first and last are written only when v > 0). Always INFO.

tests.title: NextReg snapshot at launch
tests.purpose: What state does NextZXOS / NEXLOAD leave the NextRegs in when a .nex starts: DivMMC automap registers, the 7FFD lock, the Layer 2 banks, the tilemap bases and the rest?
tests.method: As the second action at start (before any NextReg write) every NextReg $00-$FF is read through ports $243B/$253B into a 256-byte copy. The whole copy goes to the file header as R lines (R nr=$hh v=$hh) plus an H divmmc line; this test's line repeats the registers the claims name. Raw values, no timing.
tests.expect: docs/BRIEFING.md:373/:381: NEXLOAD is asked to reset NextRegs, list unconfirmed. docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:34: NextZXOS leaves $0A = $11 (automap on); claim: $B8 = $82; :35: $BB = $CD at reset (bit 7 set). docs/BRIEFING.md:117, docs/LEARNINGS.md:882: paging unlocked at launch ($08 bit 7 reads 1). lesson.loader-clears-turbosound-bit: loader clears $08 bit 1. book ch 14 (D-N1): $12 = 8, $13 = 11 at reset; docs/LEARNINGS.md:128: NextZXOS moves Layer 2 to 9-11, shadow 11-13. book ch 15 (D-N7): $6E = $2C, $6F = $0C at reset.
tests.needs: The .nex started by NEXLOAD from NextZXOS (the values are the launch state).
tests.hazard: none (reads only)
tests.fields: S01: v = NextReg $08 at launch ($hh); nr0a, nrb8, nrb9, nrba, nrbb, nr8c, nr12, nr13, nr6e, nr6f, nr05, nr07, nrc0, nrc4 = that NextReg's launch value ($hh); p7ffd = PASS if $08 bit 7 was 1 (7FFD paging unlocked), FAIL if 0. The line itself is always INFO; the 7ffd-unlocked verdict is the p7ffd key. Every NextReg's launch value is also in the header R lines (R nr=$hh v=$hh) and H divmmc line.

tests.title: core version, board id
tests.purpose: Which core version and board does the machine report: NextReg $01 / $0E as a.b.cc, machine id $00 and board id $0F?
tests.method: From the launch snapshot (S01): $01 high nibble = major, low nibble = minor, $0E = sub-minor (decimal), printed a.b.cc; $00 and $0F recorded raw. Sets the core >= 3.03 flag ($01 >= $33) that later groups use for SKIPs. No timing.
tests.expect: book ch 1 (report D, 3.02 vs 3.03 L1533): $01 = $33 and $0E = $03 on core 3.03.03. docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:17: lists the core behind each register source. book ch 3 (report D-N17, B-N22): $0F identifies the board issue (3 on an Issue 5; the Issue 2 value is not stated); $00 is the machine id.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: S02: v = core version a.b.cc from $01 / $0E (word); nr00 = NextReg $00 machine id ($hh); nr0f = NextReg $0F board id ($hh); core303 = 1 if $01 >= $33 (core 3.03 or later), else 0. Always INFO.

tests.title: RAM size (page 96)
tests.purpose: On this board, is 8K RAM page 96 ($60) real separate memory, or does it wrap onto other memory (ROM / page 0)? Tells whether the board has more than 1 MB.
tests.method: Read-only, done once in the start-up preamble at 3.5 MHz: page $60 is mapped into slot 6 (NextReg $56) and a CRC-16/CCITT of its 8K taken; the same for the suite's page 0 in slot 6, and for ROM 0's first 8K read at $0000 (ports 1FFD = $00, 7FFD = $00, slot 0 = ROM). Slot 6 and ROM 3 (1FFD $04 / 7FFD $10) are put back. Page 96 is never written.
tests.expect: docs/LEARNINGS.md:127: an unexpanded Next has 1024K = pages 0-95; 2048K = pages 0-223. book ch 3 (report D-N17), ch 5 (report B-N22): Issue 2 has 1 MB (2 MB expanded), Issue 4 drops address bit 21 so high pages wrap at 2 MB, Issue 5 has 4 MB. What page 96 shows on an unexpanded Issue 2 is not stated in the sources.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (read-only)
tests.fields: S03: v = choice: wrap (page 96 CRC equals ROM 0's first 8K), alias0 (equals page 0), distinct (neither); crc96 = CRC-16 of page 96 ($hhhh); crc0 = CRC of page 0 ($hhhh); crcrom0 = CRC of ROM 0's first 8K ($hhhh). Always INFO; the same choice is in the header (ram=).

tests.title: ROM3 bytes
tests.purpose: What bytes does the ROM 3 that NextZXOS provides hold, in particular in the spare area $386E-$3CFF that Sinclair's 48K ROM fills with $FF?
tests.method: At start the program selects ROM 3 (port 1FFD = $04, 7FFD = $10, slots 0/1 as at launch). In the preamble it takes CRC-16/CCITT (init $FFFF) of $0000-$3FFF and of $386E-$3CFF; the test then reads the bytes $0038-$0050 (IM 1 entry) and $386E-$3880. No writes.
tests.expect: lesson.alt-rom-patch-location and lesson.whole-alt-rom-image: the area $386E-$3CFF of the Next's ROM 3 is NextZXOS's, not Sinclair's all-$FF block (its IM 1 handler calls $386E, other code uses $387E, $3B00-$3CFF hold data). docs/LEARNINGS.md:1023: MAME models the alt ROM as a copy of ROM 3 with data at $3B00-$3CFF.
tests.needs: The .nex started from NextZXOS (the ROM is the one NextZXOS provides).
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: S04: v = CRC-16/CCITT of ROM 3 $0000-$3FFF ($hhhh); crc386e = CRC of $386E-$3CFF ($hhhh); b0038 = the 25 bytes $0038-$0050 as one hex string; b386e = the 19 bytes $386E-$3880 as one hex string. Always INFO (no FAIL).

tests.title: NEXTREG keeps 243B select
tests.purpose: Does a NEXTREG instruction (both the n,v and the n,A forms) leave the NextReg selected on port $243B unchanged, so a following IN from $253B still reads the register that was selected?
tests.method: NEXTREG $7F,$5A; OUT $243B = $7F; NEXTREG $56,<slot 6's current page> (harmless); IN $253B. Again with LD A,page : NEXTREG $56,A. Done at the start speed (normally 3.5 MHz), then again at 28 MHz (NextReg $07 = 3); speed restored. Each IN must return $5A (NextReg $7F), not slot 6's page.
tests.expect: docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:101: NEXTREG does not change the register selected on port $243B, so hook NEXTREGs never disturb a game's own $243B/$253B access. lesson.nextreg-select-shared-state relies on the same rule.
tests.needs: nothing special (the test sets 28 MHz itself)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: S05: v = how many of the four reads were not $5A (count); r35n = read after NEXTREG n,v at the start speed ($hh); r35a = after NEXTREG n,A at the start speed; r28n / r28a = the same at 28 MHz. PASS if all four are $5A, else FAIL.

tests.title: CPU speed read-back
tests.purpose: Does reading NextReg $07 give the actual CPU speed in bits 5:4 and the programmed speed in bits 1:0?
tests.method: For each value 0, 1, 2, 3: NEXTREG $07 = value, read $07 at once through $243B/$253B, wait for the next frame start (raster line 0), read $07 again. The start speed is restored afterwards.
tests.expect: docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:36: read $07 gives bits 5:4 = actual speed, bits 1:0 = programmed speed (core zxnext.vhd; JNext composes the same).
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: S06: v = number of speeds whose after-a-frame read did not have bits 1:0 and bits 5:4 both equal to the value written (count, 0-4); i0..i3 = $07 read straight after writing 0..3 ($hh); f0..f3 = $07 read after one frame ($hh). PASS if v = 0, else FAIL; the immediate reads (i0..i3) are information only.

tests.title: SD file write + read back
tests.purpose: Can a .nex started from NextZXOS create, write, close, reopen and read back a file on the SD card through the esxDOS RST 8 calls?
tests.method: After the group, the result file NXSUITE.TXT is written (RST 8 F_OPEN $9A with mode $0E create/truncate, F_WRITE $9E per 8K page, F_CLOSE $9B) with interrupts off, MMU slots 0/1 = $FF (ROM) and a stack outside slots 0/1. It is then opened read-only (mode $01), the first 64 bytes read (F_READ $9D), closed, and compared with the text still in memory.
tests.expect: asm/inferno_hooks.asm:7553: the RST 8 call convention used (F_OPEN / F_WRITE / F_CLOSE, slots 0/1 = $FF, interrupts off, own stack). games/inferno.md:260: such esxDOS saves work in JNext; hardware to confirm. Prediction: the file is written and reads back equal.
tests.needs: The .nex started from a writable SD card folder (files go to the current drive and folder); DivMMC automap on as NextZXOS leaves it.
tests.hazard: Writes to the SD card: it rewrites the suite's own result file NXSUITE.TXT in the start folder (claim: could corrupt SD or settings; writes one file only). Not opt-in.
tests.fields: S07: v = 64 when the file was written, reopened read-only and its first 64 bytes equal the text in memory, else 0 (count of bytes compared). PASS if they match, FAIL if any step failed (write, open, short read or a differing byte); a FAIL means the result file may be missing, so the screen shows it (photograph).

tests.title: 28 MHz SRAM fetch
tests.purpose: At 28 MHz, do instructions running from ordinary SRAM take extra wait states on memory reads (core 3.02) or the same CPU clocks as at 3.5 MHz (core 3.03)?
tests.method: At NextReg $07 = 3 (28 MHz), code in bank 2 ($B000), data in RAM page 56 in slot 3 ($6000): blocks of NOP, LD A,($6000), POP BC (SP = $6000), LD (IX+5),$AA, and one LDIR of 2048 bytes ($6000 -> $6800). Timed with the raster line counter over 2048 x 8 instructions, minus an empty block, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration; 5 runs. Result: 28 MHz clocks per instruction (per byte for LDIR). $07 read back after the runs.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D L1861, L1921, L5172): core 3.03 has no wait at 28 MHz: NOP 4, LD A,(nn) 13, POP BC 10, LD (IX+d),n 19 clocks (spec: LDIR 21 per byte); core 3.02: 5 / 17 / 13 / 23. lesson.core-302-read-wait-state-gone-in-303: the read wait belongs to 3.02. docs/TECHNIQUES.md:57: each memory read adds a wait state, 28 MHz is ~6.3-7x 3.5 MHz (written from 3.02 measurements).
tests.needs: nothing special (the test sets 28 MHz itself)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C01: v = NOP clocks at 28 MHz (mean of 5 runs, with min / max); nop, lda, pop, ldixn, ldir = mean 28 MHz clocks per NOP, LD A,(nn), POP BC, LD (IX+d),n and per LDIR byte; nr07 = NextReg $07 read back after the runs ($hh); choice = no-wait / wait / other. PASS (choice no-wait) if all five rows are within 0.2 of 4 / 13 / 10 / 19 / 21; otherwise INFO with choice wait if NOP is 5 +- 0.2, else other.

tests.title: 28 MHz bank 5
tests.purpose: At 28 MHz, do code fetches and data reads in bank 5 (block RAM, pages $0A/$0B) take a wait state?
tests.method: At 28 MHz ($07 = 3): a NOP block (256 copies) built at $6800 in bank 5 and its empty block at $6B00, timed with the raster line counter (2048 x 8 NOPs, 4 passes, minus empty, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs). Then LD A,(HL) with HL = $4000 (bank 5) from a block in bank 2. Result: 28 MHz clocks per instruction.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D L1921, L2543): on 3.02 reads from bank 5 waited like SRAM; 3.03 is not measured by the book. lesson.core-302-read-wait-state-gone-in-303: no read wait on 3.03. Claim: on 3.03 no wait state in bank 5 (NOP 4 clocks).
tests.needs: nothing special (the test sets 28 MHz itself)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C02: v = NOP clocks at 28 MHz with the code in bank 5 ($6800) (mean of 5 runs, min / max); ldhl = mean 28 MHz clocks per LD A,(HL) with HL = $4000 in bank 5 and the code in bank 2. Always INFO.

tests.title: 28 MHz page $0E
tests.purpose: At 28 MHz, do code fetches and data reads in page $0E (block RAM, first half of bank 7) take a wait state?
tests.method: Page $0E is mapped into slot 3 ($6000-$7FFF). At 28 MHz a NOP block is built at $6000 in that page (empty block at $6300) and timed with the raster line counter (2048 x 8 NOPs, 4 passes, minus empty, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs); then LD A,(HL) with HL = $6000 in that page from a block in bank 2. Slot 3 restored. Result: 28 MHz clocks per instruction.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D L1921, L2543): reads from page $0E never had the 28 MHz wait, on 3.02 and on 3.03 (NOP 4 clocks).
tests.needs: nothing special (page $0E belongs to bank 7, which is in the .nex)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C03: v = NOP clocks at 28 MHz with the code in page $0E (mean of 5 runs, min / max); ldhl = mean 28 MHz clocks per LD A,(HL) reading page $0E, code in bank 2. Always INFO.

tests.title: 28 MHz page $0F
tests.purpose: At 28 MHz, do code fetches and data reads in page $0F (second half of bank 7, ordinary SRAM) take a wait state?
tests.method: As C03 with page $0F in slot 3: at 28 MHz a NOP block at $6000 in page $0F (empty block at $6300), timed with the raster line counter (2048 x 8 NOPs, 4 passes, minus empty, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs); then LD A,(HL) with HL = $6000 in that page, code in bank 2. Slot 3 restored. Result: 28 MHz clocks per instruction.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D L2543): page $0F is ordinary SRAM: it waited at 28 MHz on 3.02 (NOP 5), no wait on 3.03 (NOP 4).
tests.needs: nothing special (page $0F belongs to bank 7, which is in the .nex)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C04: v = NOP clocks at 28 MHz with the code in page $0F (mean of 5 runs, min / max); ldhl = mean 28 MHz clocks per LD A,(HL) reading page $0F, code in bank 2. Always INFO.

tests.title: 28 MHz writes / IO
tests.purpose: At 28 MHz, do memory writes and I/O instructions take the extra wait state that 3.02 put on reads?
tests.method: At 28 MHz, code in bank 2: blocks of LD (HL),A (HL = $6000 in RAM page 56), OUT (C),A with BC = $243B and A = $7F (selects NextReg $7F), and IN A,(C) with BC = $253B, each timed with the raster line counter (2048 x 8, 4 passes, minus an empty block, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs). Result: 28 MHz clocks per instruction, to compare with the instruction's 3.5 MHz T.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D L1921): the 3.02 28 MHz wait applied to memory reads only (opcode, operand, data), not to writes or I/O. lesson.core-302-read-wait-state-gone-in-303: no read wait at all on 3.03. Clock numbers per instruction are not stated in the sources.
tests.needs: nothing special (the test sets 28 MHz itself)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C05: v = 28 MHz clocks per LD (HL),A (mean of 5 runs, min / max); outc = mean clocks per OUT (C),A to port $243B; inc = mean clocks per IN A,(C) from port $253B. Always INFO.

tests.title: 7 / 14 MHz scaling
tests.purpose: At 7 and 14 MHz, do instructions take the same number of CPU clocks as at 3.5 MHz?
tests.method: The C01 rows (NOP, LD A,(nn), POP BC, LD (IX+d),n, LDIR per byte; code in bank 2, data in RAM page 56 at $6000) run at NextReg $07 = 1 (7 MHz) and then $07 = 2 (14 MHz), each timed with the raster line counter (block called 8 x 2^speed times, 4 passes, minus empty, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs). Result: clocks of that speed per instruction.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D L1915), ch 3 (report D-N21): at 7 and 14 MHz instructions take the same CPU clocks as at 3.5 MHz (contention is gone above 3.5 MHz); the book gives about 8x over the four speeds on 3.03 and about 6.5x on 3.02.
tests.needs: nothing special (the test sets the speeds itself)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C06: v = NOP clocks at 7 MHz (mean of 5 runs, min / max); nop7, lda7, pop7, ldixn7, ldir7 = mean 7 MHz clocks per NOP, LD A,(nn), POP BC, LD (IX+d),n and per LDIR byte; nop14, lda14, pop14, ldixn14, ldir14 = the same at 14 MHz. Always INFO.

tests.title: speed switch cost
tests.purpose: How much time does a NEXTREG $07 speed switch cost, and does the new speed take effect at once?
tests.method: From 3.5 MHz: a block of 64 x (NEXTREG $07,3 ; NEXTREG $07,0) called twice (128 pairs) is timed against a block of 64 x (NEXTREG $07,0 ; NEXTREG $07,0) called twice, with the raster line counter (4 passes, 5 runs, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration). Result: extra time per pair in 3.5 MHz T. A difference below zero is recorded as 0 (the timing core clamps it).
tests.expect: lesson.speed-switch-cost-calibrate-at-boot: timing constants that include a speed switch need the machine's own figure (calibrated at boot in Inferno; the repo value is unknown). docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:36: $07 bits 1:0 set the speed. Claim: the switch takes effect at once and costs only its own 20 T.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C07: v = extra 3.5 MHz T per (NEXTREG 7,3 ; NEXTREG 7,0) pair compared with a (NEXTREG 7,0 ; NEXTREG 7,0) pair (mean of 5 runs, min / max; T; a pair faster than the reference reads 0). Always INFO.

tests.title: bank 5 contention
tests.purpose: At 3.5 MHz, are reads from bank 5 slowed (contended) during the display, does NextReg $08 bit 6 = 1 turn that off, and is it gone at 7 MHz?
tests.method: LD A,(HL) x 2048 from a block in bank 2, started at raster line 0 (inside the display), HL = $4000 (bank 5) against HL = $8000 (bank 2); raster-line timing scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs. Repeated with $08 bit 6 set (read-modify-write, bit 7 written 0, restored after), and again at 7 MHz. Result: extra T per access (bank 5 minus bank 2).
tests.expect: book ch 3 (report D-N21), ch 5 (report B-N2): at 3.5 MHz in 48K/128K timing bank 5 is contended during the display (claim: up to 6 T per access); not at 7 MHz and above; 48K: bank 5, 128K: banks 1,3,5,7, +3: 4-7, only pages $00-$0F. docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:37: $08 bit 6 = 1 disables contention. docs/LEARNINGS.md:30, lesson.beeper-contention: contention matters for beam racing and beeper timing.
tests.needs: nothing special; the result is for the machine timing in use (the claim is about 48K/128K timing)
tests.hazard: none (NextReg $08 bit 6 is changed and restored)
tests.fields: C08: v = extra T per LD A,(HL) access, bank 5 minus bank 2, at 3.5 MHz during the display (difference of the 5-run means; n = 5, min = max = v; T; can be negative); off = the same with $08 bit 6 = 1 (contention off); c7 = the same at 7 MHz (in 7 MHz clocks). Always INFO.

tests.title: $08 bit 6 latch
tests.purpose: After a write to NextReg $08 bit 6 (contention off), when does reading $08 back show the new bit: at once, or only from dot 256 of the line?
tests.method: At 3.5 MHz, interrupts off: at the start of raster line L (L = 20..27, one sample each) the program writes $08 with bit 6 flipped (bit 7 written 0), then reads $08 through $253B 24 times, 23 T apart (unrolled IN), then restores bit 6. A sample = T from the NEXTREG to the first read that shows the new bit (999 if none of the 24 does). Result in T.
tests.expect: book ch 3 (report D-N21): the ULA samples NextReg $08 bit 6 only from dot 256 of each line, and $08 reads back the old bit until then.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (NextReg $08 bit 6 is changed and restored)
tests.fields: 8 samples (lines 20-27, the write at the start of the line): T from the NEXTREG $08 write to the first read (reads 23 T apart) that shows the new bit 6; v = max, min, t0 = how many were 0. Board run 5: v=23 min=0 t0=2 - the new bit is read back by the first or the second read every time (two populations = which side of the change the first read lands): the read-back follows the write within 23 T, it does not keep the old bit until dot 256 of the line.

tests.title: IO contention
tests.purpose: At 3.5 MHz, is an IN from an even port (the ULA's $FE) slowed (I/O-contended) during the display compared with the border?
tests.method: At 3.5 MHz: 1024 x IN A,($FE) with A = $FF (port $FFFE) in a block in bank 2, timed with the raster line counter (4 passes, minus empty, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs), started at line 0 (display) and again started at line 193 (border, ending before line 243). Result: T per IN.
tests.expect: book ch 3 (report D-N21): in 48K/128K timing every even port (and $7FFD in 128K timing) is I/O-contended at 3.5 MHz, so the display figure should be larger than the border figure. Exact T values are not stated in the sources.
tests.needs: nothing special; the result is for the machine timing in use (the claim is about 48K/128K timing)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C10: v = T per IN A,($FE) started at line 0, inside the display (mean of 5 runs, min / max; T); border = mean T per IN started at line 193, in the border. Always INFO.

tests.title: undocumented opcode T
tests.purpose: How long do undocumented opcodes take: an unlisted ED opcode (ED 00), the ED forms of LD (nn),HL / LD HL,(nn) (ED 63 / ED 6B), and a DD prefix before an instruction that does not use HL?
tests.method: At 3.5 MHz, code in bank 2, timed with the raster line counter (256 copies x 8 calls, 4 passes, minus empty, scaled by the calibration, 5 runs): blocks of ED 00, ED 63 $6000, ED 6B $6000 (address in RAM page 56) and DD 00 (DD + NOP). Result: T per instruction.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D-N29): every unlisted ED opcode is an 8 T NOP; ED 63 / ED 6B take 4 T more than LD (nn),HL / LD HL,(nn) (spec: 20 T, LD (nn),HL being 16); a DD/FD prefix before a non-HL instruction costs 4 T (DD 00 = 8 T). docs/LEARNINGS.md:50: on the Next 29 ED opcodes are Z80N instructions, the rest NOPs.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: C11: v = T per ED 00 (mean of 5 runs, min / max; T); ed63 = mean T per ED 63 nn; ed6b = mean T per ED 6B nn; dd00 = mean T per DD 00 (DD prefix + NOP). Always INFO.

tests.title: undocumented flags X/Y
tests.purpose: How are the undocumented flag bits 5 and 3 (Y/X) set by BIT n,(HL), SCF, CCF, CPI, IN r,(C) and LD A,I on the Next?

tests.hazard: none

Always INFO.

tests.title: Layer 2 vs CPU waits
tests.purpose: Does a visible Layer 2 picture slow the CPU at 28 MHz (does Layer 2 display fetching ever make the CPU wait)?
tests.method: At 28 MHz, started at raster line 0: LDIR of 1K from $8000 (bank 2) to $F000 (bank 0), 8 times, timed with the raster line counter (4 passes, minus empty, scaled by the 3.5 MHz calibration, 5 runs) with Layer 2 off, then with a 320x256 Layer 2 visible (NextReg $12 = 22, $70 = $10, $69 bit 7 set). $12, $70, $69 restored to the launch values. Result: 28 MHz clocks per byte.

tests.needs: nothing special (uses suite bank 22 for the picture)
tests.hazard: none (Layer 2 is shown briefly; registers restored)
tests.fields: C15: v = 28 MHz clocks per LDIR byte with 320x256 Layer 2 visible (mean of 5 runs, min / max); off = mean clocks per byte with Layer 2 off. PASS if the two differ by no more than 0.05 clock, else INFO.

tests.title: z80ntest FUNC cases
tests.purpose: Do the Z80N instructions give the register, memory and flag results that the toolkit's model (nexclash/z80n.py) predicts, including LDIX-family flags, LDPIRX, JP (C) and TEST n's N flag?
tests.method: At 3.5 MHz, interrupts off, slots 6/7 = sandbox pages: the 46 z80ntest FUNC cases. Each runs one Z80N instruction from known A F BC DE HL, SP = $6200 and a 1 KB window at $6000; flag-changing ones from F = 0 and F = $FF, others from F = $A5. A..L, SP, F and a Fletcher checksum of the window are compared with values generated from nexclash/z80n.py. NEXTREG / OUTINB cases read NextReg $7F back; JP (C) uses a slot table at $C000.
tests.expect: tools/hwtests/README.md:59/:82, docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:115: expected values are z80n.py's (from core 3.02.05 VHDL). docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:131: LDIX family flags change like LDI/LDIR incl. bits 5/3 (CSpect keeps 5/3: docs/LEARNINGS.md:1005). :133: LDPIRX wrong on 3.02.00, fixed in 3.02.02. :117: JP (C) leaves flags unchanged (also book D-C3); :135 calls them undefined; CSpect sets IN-style flags. :136: TEST n = AND flags, A kept; NF 0 in Ped7g's table, unknown elsewhere.

tests.hazard: none

One sub-line per case, id zf.<case> (name without spaces; a last character 0 / F = run from F = 0 / $FF): v = F after ($hh); f = F after ($hh); fexp = F expected ($hh); code = R (a register or SP differs), M (memory checksum differs) or F (only F differs), written only when the case did not match. Sub-line PASS if everything matches, else FAIL.

tests.title: ADD rr,A carry
tests.purpose: Does ADD HL/DE/BC,A always clear the carry flag (even when the add wraps) and keep the other flags, and does ADD HL,nn leave the flags alone?
tests.method: Each case runs once at the start speed from code in bank 5, interrupts off, F recorded: ADD HL,A with HL = $1000, A = $20 (no wrap); HL = $FFF0, A = $20 (wrap); ADD DE,A and ADD BC,A with $FFF0 + $20 (wrap); ADD HL,$1234 with HL = $F000 (wrap); every case from F = 0 and from F = $FF.
tests.expect: lesson.z80n-add-rr-a-and-ldws-carry-unsettled and docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:117 (from the core VHDL): ADD rr,A sets CF = 0. docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:126: carry not preserved (undefined/reset per the wiki). book ch 2 (report D-C1): clears CF. docs/LEARNINGS.md:1005: CSpect keeps CF. Claim: ADD rr,nn leaves all flags.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: Z02: v = how many of the 8 ADD rr,A cases had CF set after (count); f1..fA = F after each case ($hh): f1/f2 ADD HL,A no wrap from F = 0 / $FF, f3/f4 ADD HL,A wrap, f5/f6 ADD DE,A wrap, f7/f8 ADD BC,A wrap, f9/fA ADD HL,$1234 (recorded, not judged); choice = clears-CF (CF 0 after all 8), keeps-CF (CF after = CF before in all 8), other. PASS if clears-CF, else INFO.

tests.title: LDWS flags
tests.purpose: Which flags does LDWS set: those of ADD D,1 (carry set when D was $FF) or those of INC D (carry kept)?
tests.method: LDWS (ED A5) runs once per case at the start speed from code in bank 5, interrupts off, with HL = $F000, E = $10 and D = $7F or $FF, each from F = 0 and from F = $FF (the copy lands at $7F10 / $FF10). F after is recorded. The carry after the cases D = $7F from F = $FF and D = $FF from F = 0 decides.
tests.expect: docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:134: flags of ADD D,1 (CF = D was $FF); z80n.py expects $94 (D = $7F from F = $FF) and $51 (D = $FF from F = 0) per tools/hwtests/README.md. book ch 2 (report D-C2): INC D flags (carry kept). docs/LEARNINGS.md:1005: CSpect uses INC D flags ($95 / $50). lesson.z80n-add-rr-a-and-ldws-carry-unsettled: do not rely on carry after LDWS.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: Z03: v = choice: ADD-D-1 (no carry for D = $7F from F = $FF and carry for D = $FF from F = 0), INC-D (carry kept: the reverse), other; f1..f4 = F after ($hh) for D = $7F from F = 0, D = $7F from F = $FF, D = $FF from F = 0, D = $FF from F = $FF; choice = the same word. Always INFO.

tests.title: ED B6 sandbox
tests.purpose: What does the unlisted opcode ED B6 do on the Next: the same as LDIRX, nothing, or something else?
tests.method: In a guarded scratch area in the suite's own page ($F000-$F1FF filled with $AA): source $F010 = 11 22 E3 44 55 66 77 88, destination $F110 = 8 zeros; HL = $F010, DE = $F110, BC = 8, A = $E3, F = 0, alternate registers 0, interrupts off. ED B6 is executed once (from bank 5 code); HL, DE, BC and $F100-$F127 are saved. The area is reset and LDIRX (ED B4) run the same way for comparison.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D-C5): ED B6 behaves exactly like LDIRX. docs/LEARNINGS.md:647: the repo treats it as unknown (an unfinished LDIRSCALE): z80n.py raises Z80NError on ED B6 and it is never executed in builds.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (the claim notes it could corrupt memory inside the guarded sandbox only)
tests.fields: Z04: v = choice: same-as-LDIRX (HL, DE, BC and the 40 bytes $F100-$F127 equal LDIRX's), NOP (HL, DE, BC unchanged and the 8 destination bytes still 0), other; hl, de, bc = the registers after ED B6 ($hhhh); dst = the 8 destination bytes after ED B6 as one hex string; choice = the same word. Always INFO.

tests.title: PIXELDN / PIXELAD edges
tests.purpose: What do PIXELDN and PIXELAD return at the edges of the ULA screen: PIXELDN past the last pixel row, PIXELAD with a row number of 192 or more?
tests.method: Each case runs once at the start speed from code in bank 5, interrupts off, and HL after is recorded: PIXELDN (ED 93) from HL = $57FF and $57E0; PIXELAD (ED 94) with D = 192, 200, 255 and E = 0 and 255.
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D-N27): PIXELDN past row 191 runs on into the attribute area. docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:130: PIXELAD is undefined for D >= 192 (it always returns a $4000-based address).
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: Z05: v = 8 (number of cases, count); dn57ff, dn57e0 = HL after PIXELDN from $57FF / $57E0 ($hhhh); ad192_0, ad192_255, ad200_0, ad200_255, ad255_0, ad255_255 = HL after PIXELAD with D = 192 / 200 / 255 and E = 0 / 255 ($hhhh). Always INFO.

tests.title: Z80N T-states 3.5 MHz
tests.purpose: Does every Z80N instruction take the T-states of the documented table at 3.5 MHz?
tests.method: At 3.5 MHz, slots 6/7 = sandbox pages (reads $D0xx, writes $E0xx, stack $F000): the 31 z80ntest TIME cases (Z80 controls NEG, LDI, LDIR first). Each block is 256 copies called 8 times (or one repeating instruction with BC = 2048), timed with the raster line counter against its base block, 4 passes a quarter line apart, 5 runs, scaled by the calibration (2048 x LD A,(IX+0) = 19 T each). Result: T per instruction.
tests.expect: docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:121 table (also z80n.OPCODES), tools/hwtests/README.md:82: e.g. LDWS 14, PUSH nn 23, NEXTREG 20 / 17, TEST 11, LDIX 16, repeats 21 / 16; controls NEG 8, LDI 16, LDIR 21. book ch 2 (report D-N30): all 29 agree with the table. docs/LEARNINGS.md:1005: CSpect takes 19 T for PUSH nn.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: Z06: v = number of TIME cases within 0.5 T of the table (count, of 31). PASS if all 31; FAIL otherwise; if one of the controls NEG / LDI / LDIR failed the line also says method=fail (the method, not the Z80N rows, failed). One sub-line per case, id zt.<name> (spaces removed): v = mean T per instruction over 5 runs with min / max (written with unit clocks; at 3.5 MHz these are T); exp = expected T from the table. Sub-line PASS if within 0.5 of exp, else FAIL.

tests.title: Z80N clocks 28 MHz
tests.purpose: At 28 MHz, do the Z80N instructions take the same number of CPU clocks as at 3.5 MHz (no read wait state, core 3.03)?
tests.method: The Z06 blocks (31 TIME cases, same sandbox pages) run at NextReg $07 = 3 (28 MHz); each block is called 8 times as often as at 3.5 MHz (4 passes, 5 runs) against its base block, and the raster lines are converted with the 3.5 MHz calibration. Result: 28 MHz clocks per instruction.

tests.needs: nothing special (the test sets 28 MHz itself)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: Z07: v = number of TIME cases within 0.5 clock of the 3.5 MHz table (count, of 31). PASS if all 31, else INFO (a number, not a verdict; no method=fail here). One sub-line per case, id zu.<name> (spaces removed): v = mean 28 MHz clocks per instruction over 5 runs with min / max (clocks); exp = the 3.5 MHz T from the table. Sub-line PASS if within 0.5 of exp, else INFO.

tests.title: pulse IM2 bus $FF
tests.purpose: In pulse interrupt mode, which byte does the CPU read from the data bus when it accepts an interrupt? The claim is $FF, so IM 2 takes its handler address from I*256+$FF.
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode, ULA frame interrupt only. IM 2 with I = $FA and a 257-byte table at $FA00-$FB00 filled with $F9 except $FAFF/$FB00 = $F8: a bus byte of $FF reaches handler A at $F8F8, any other byte reaches handler B at $F9F9 (the spec's I = $90 layout moved to a free page). Interrupts on for 5 frames (counted by polling the raster at line 150); each handler counts its runs. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: lesson.pulse-mode-im2-bus-reads-ff: the acknowledge reads $FF, IM 2 vector = I*256+$FF, IM 0 acts as IM 1; a device on an enabled expansion bus can put its own byte there. docs/BRIEFING.md:434: unconfirmed on every core, but relied on. docs/BRIEFING.md:424: context (Cyclone's I = $3A table). book ch 4 (report A-N, D-N22): the FPGA drives $FF (the expansion bus may override).
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I01: v = runs of handler A, the $FF-bus handler, over 5 frames (count); b = runs of handler B (any other bus byte). PASS if b = 0 and v is 4-6, else FAIL.

tests.title: IM 2 by ED 7E
tests.purpose: Does the undocumented opcode ED 7E switch the CPU into interrupt mode 2?
tests.method: Same set-up as I01 (28 MHz, pulse mode, I = $FA table where a $FF bus byte reaches counting handler A). The CPU is put in IM 1, then ED 7E is executed instead of IM 2. Interrupts on for 5 frames. If ED 7E did not select IM 2, the ROM handler at $0038 runs instead and handler A never counts. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: docs/LEARNINGS.md:46: ED 7E sets IM 2 only from core 3.01.08 on (core changelog); older cores misbehave with games that use it.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I02: v = runs of handler A over 5 frames (count); b = runs of handler B (a bus byte other than $FF). PASS if b = 0 and v is 4-6, else FAIL.

tests.title: im2hold T1-T7
tests.purpose: Repeats the earlier im2hold board test inside the suite: does hardware IM2 mode hold an interrupt until RETI, lose it in pulse mode, and block later interrupts after a handler that ends with plain RET?
tests.method: 28 MHz. Seven sub-tests in the order T1 T2 T3 T5 T6 T4 T7: T1 ULA vector read from I*256+$16 (hardware table I = $FC); T2 an interrupt during 3 frames of DI is taken at EI (hardware IM2); T3 the same in pulse mode is lost; T5 a RETI trampoline to a game-style EI;RET handler; T6 a uniform 257-byte table (I = $FD); T4 a handler ending EI;RET (never acknowledged); T7 one dummy RETI with interrupts off, then 5 frames. Results are handler run counts.
tests.expect: tools/hwtests/README.md:19 (im2hold table): T1 vector I*256+$16; T2 held and taken at EI; T3 lost in pulse mode; T4 info; T5, T6, T7 4-6 runs in 5 frames. docs/BRIEFING.md:415 and docs/TECHNIQUES.md:596: hardware IM2 holds each interrupt until a RETI acknowledges it. lesson.frame-overrun-lost-interrupts: an interrupt spanned with interrupts off is missed (pulse mode). Book (claim values): agrees, held, RET blocks.
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode (set by the test)
tests.hazard: Could hang: T4 leaves an interrupt unacknowledged, blocking later ones until T7's dummy RETI. The progress record is marked first: if the machine stops, the next start resumes and marks the test HANG-GUARD. Interrupt state is restored after.
tests.fields: I03: v = number of sub-tests that passed (count); one extra line per sub-test, ids ih.t1 .. ih.t7, each v = im2hold's detail byte: t1 = 1 on pass, else runs of a wrong-vector handler; t2 = interrupts taken after the EI; t3 = interrupts taken (0 = lost); t4 = runs of the EI;RET handler (1 = RET does not acknowledge, up to 200 = re-fires); t5, t6, t7 = handler runs in 5 frames. Sub status: t1 PASS if no wrong handler ran and the right one ran; t2 PASS if > 0; t3 PASS if 0; t4 always INFO; t5-t7 PASS if 4-6. Main line FAIL if any sub-test failed, else PASS.

tests.title: pulse length 3.5 MHz
tests.purpose: How long does the pulse-mode /INT signal stay low at 3.5 MHz, measured as how soon after the acknowledge a handler may re-enable interrupts without being entered a second time?
tests.method: 3.5 MHz, pulse mode IM 2. The handler is built in RAM: INC IX (10 T, counts runs), k T of padding (NOP, INC DE, LD D,0, LD R,A mixes), EI, 4 NOPs, RET. k is swept 0 and 4..60 T (k = 1-3 and 5 cannot be built). 5 frames per k; 7 or more runs in 5 frames = re-entry. Part 2: a handler of 9 IN reads of NextReg $22 (12 T apart from its first instruction) counts how many leading reads see bit 7 (/INT low) set. Result in T.
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-C2): 32 T in 48K/+3 timing, 36 T in 128K/Pentagon. docs/TECHNIQUES.md:251: the ULA pulse lasts ~30 T at 3.5 MHz. docs/BRIEFING.md:111 and lesson.interrupt-handler-runs-twice-next-core: /INT outlasts a 128K's 36 T; an instruction after EI ending 38 T after the acknowledge re-enters, 42 T does not. lesson.int-pulse-length-unsettled: open question; keep handlers longer than 42 T before EI.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: Could hang: an early-EI handler is re-entered; sources switched off after 2047 runs. The progress record is marked first: if the machine stops, the next start resumes and marks the test HANG-GUARD. Interrupt state is restored after.
tests.fields: I04: v = the largest padding k (T at 3.5 MHz, after the 10 T INC IX) for which the handler re-entered (-1 = no k re-entered) (T); reentered = how many k values re-entered; hi22 = the most leading NextReg $22 reads (of 9, 12 T apart from the handler's first instruction) with bit 7 set, over 5 frames; skip = k1-3,5 (padding values that cannot be built). Always INFO.

tests.title: pulse length 7-28 MHz
tests.purpose: Is the pulse-mode /INT length a fixed number of CPU clocks at every CPU speed (so 8x shorter in real time at 28 MHz)?
tests.method: The I04 re-entry sweep repeated at NextReg $07 = 1, 2 and 3 (7, 14, 28 MHz), handler and foreground at that speed: padding k from 0 to 60 x 2^speed clocks in steps of 2^speed; 7+ runs in 5 frames = re-entry. Part 2 at each speed: 9 handler reads of NextReg $22, how many leading reads see bit 7 set. Results in CPU clocks of that speed.
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-C2): the pulse is counted in CPU clocks, the same number at every speed (32 / 36 by timing, as I04). lesson.int-pulse-length-unsettled: the length is an open question (book 32 / 36 T; a board saw re-entry 38 T after the acknowledge).
tests.needs: 7, 14 and 28 MHz (set by the test)
tests.hazard: Could hang: an early-EI handler is re-entered; sources switched off after 2047 runs. The progress record is marked first: if the machine stops, the next start resumes and marks the test HANG-GUARD. Interrupt state is restored after.
tests.fields: I05: v = the largest re-entering padding k at 28 MHz (clocks of 28 MHz, after the INC IX; -1 = none) (clocks); k7 / k14 = the same at 7 and 14 MHz (clocks of that speed); hi22_7 / hi22_14 / hi22_28 = the most leading NextReg $22 reads (of 9) with bit 7 set at each speed. Always INFO.

tests.title: HW IM2 vector layout
tests.purpose: In hardware IM2 mode, which vector byte does each interrupt source put on the bus: $C0 bits 7:5, then the 4-bit source index, then 0?
tests.method: 28 MHz, hardware IM2 with $C0 = $E1 (vector bits 7:5 = 111, bit 3 kept as found), I = $FC, 16 distinct handlers at $FCE0-$FCFF (the rest of the table points to a 'wrong' handler). Three runs, one source each, 3 frames: the ULA frame interrupt; the line interrupt at line 100 ($22/$23, $C4 bit 1); CTC0 as a timer with time constant 255 and its interrupt on ($C5 bit 0). The handler that ran gives the vector offset (a byte).
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-N): line $E0, CTC0 $E6, ULA $F6 (CTC 4-7 reserved, never fire). lesson.pulse-mode-im2-bus-reads-ff: context (pulse mode reads $FF). docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:86: vectors line 0 (highest), CTC 3-10, ULA 11. tools/hwtests/README.md:27: with bits 7:5 = 000 the ULA handler is read from I*256+$16.
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I06: v = vector offset of the handler the ULA interrupt ran ($hh; $FF = none ran); line = the offset for the line interrupt; ctc0 = the offset for CTC0; wrong = runs of handlers outside $FCE0-$FCFF during the last (CTC0) run. PASS if v = $F6, else INFO.

tests.title: status bits $C8
tests.purpose: Does NextReg $C8 record a ULA interrupt even when it was missed under DI, is it cleared by writing 1 and left alone by writing 0?
tests.method: 28 MHz. Pulse mode: a whole frame with interrupts off (two passes of line 150), read $C8 (and $C0, $C4, $22 as they were), write $C8 = 0 and read, write $C8 = 1 and read. Hardware IM2: a whole frame under DI, read $C8, write 1, read. Results are raw register bytes.

tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I07: v = $C8 after a pulse-mode frame under DI ($hh); pdi = the same; pw0 = $C8 after writing 0; pw1 = $C8 after writing 1; hdi = $C8 after a hardware-IM2 frame under DI; hw1 = after writing 1 there; c0 / c4 / nr22 = NextRegs $C0, $C4, $22 at the time of the pulse-mode read. PASS if bit 0 of pdi / pw0 / pw1 is 1 / 1 / 0, else FAIL (the hardware pair is recorded only).

tests.title: $22 bit 7 /INT time
tests.purpose: How long does NextReg $22 bit 7 (/INT asserted) read 1 in pulse mode, for the frame interrupt and for a line interrupt?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode, interrupts off. $22 is selected once; wait for bit 7 = 0 then = 1 (a read every ~49 clocks), then 128 unrolled reads 23 clocks apart are stored; high time = (1 + leading reads with bit 7 set) x 23 clocks. 5 pulses of the ULA frame interrupt, then 5 of a line interrupt at line 100 ($C4 bit 1). Results in clocks of 28 MHz (resolution 23).

tests.needs: 28 MHz (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I08: v = the longest time $22 bit 7 read 1 for the ULA interrupt over 5 pulses (clocks of 28 MHz, steps of 23); min / max = shortest / longest of the 5; n = 5; line = the longest for the line-100 interrupt; linemin = its shortest. 0 = bit 7 never seen set. Always INFO.

tests.title: ULA interrupt line
tests.purpose: On which raster line does the ULA frame interrupt arrive, and is it the same line every frame?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode IM 2. CTC3 runs free (prescaler 16, constant 256). For 250 frames the handler reads the raster line ($1F, $1E, $1F: LSB, MSB, LSB) and then the CTC3 count, a few clocks after the acknowledge; the smallest and largest of each are kept. Line in raster lines; CTC phase in raw CTC3 counts.

tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I09: v = the smallest raster line read in the handler (lines); min / max = smallest / largest line over the run; n = handler runs (about 250); ctcmin / ctcmax = smallest / largest CTC3 count read just after the line (phase within the line). Always INFO.

tests.title: line interrupt position
tests.purpose: Where exactly is the line interrupt for line N raised: on line N-1, how many T before line N starts?
tests.method: 3.5 MHz, hardware IM2, line interrupt only, CTC3 free running (prescaler 16: one tick = 2 T). Interrupts off, wait for line N-2, poll the line LSB until it reads N-1 and read CTC3; then EI and wait until the handler (first thing: read CTC3) has run. The CTC difference, corrected for fixed instruction costs and minus the line length, gives the interrupt position against the start of line N in T. 5 samples each at N = 0, 100, 191 and the last line - 2.
tests.expect: lesson.line-interrupt-fires-on-previous-line: raised on line n-1 at dot 243 of its display area, a little over 100 T before line n at 3.5 MHz. docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:85: it fires as the previous line's pixels end. book ch 10 (report A-N): line n-1 dot 243.
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: pN = T at 3.5 MHz from the line interrupt for line N to the moment the raster counter ($1E / $1F) reads N (negative = before), mean of 5; sN = spread of the 5 raw readings (above ~24 T = not repeatable). Board run 5: mid-frame p100=-150 s100=0 and p191=-149 s191=2 - the interrupt comes 150 T (+-12) before the counter reads N, i.e. 78 T after the counter read N-1 (a 228 T line), repeatable; near the frame end it moves and spreads (p0=-7 s0=88, plast2=-122 s50): those two lines sit next to the counter's wrap at the frame end, where this test's own sync waits cross the frame boundary - read them as 'not constant there', not as a position.

tests.title: line interrupt numbering
tests.purpose: How are line-interrupt numbers counted at the end of the frame: does one past the last line act as line 0, and do higher values never fire?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode IM 2, ULA interrupt off, line interrupt on ($22 bit 1 and bit 0 = MSB, $23 = LSB, $C4 = 2). Three runs of 5 frames: line = last+1, last+2 and 511, where last = the largest raster line measured at start-up. The handler counts runs and records the smallest raster line it read. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: book ch 4/10 (report A-N): numbers follow the raster count ($64 = 0: display row 0 = line 0, through the border to the frame end); a value one past the last line acts as line 0; higher values never fire; 9 bits ($22 bit 0 + $23). lesson.line-interrupt-fires-on-previous-line: line n is raised on line n-1.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I11: v = handler runs over 5 frames with the line interrupt set to last+1 (count); line = the smallest raster line read in that handler (65535 = never ran); last2 / line2 = the same for last+2; l511 / line3 = the same for 511; at = the line number used for last+1. PASS if last+2 and 511 never fire and last+1 fires 4-6 times at line 0 or at the last line (raised on the line before), else FAIL.

tests.title: CTC rate per speed
tests.purpose: Does the CTC count at a fixed rate from the 28 MHz clock, whatever the CPU speed?
tests.method: Interrupts off. At NextReg $07 = 0, 1, 2, 3 in turn: CTC3 free running with prescaler 256 and constant 256; count its ticks (wraps tracked by polling) over 8 frames, from one fall of the raster line MSB to the 8th. Result in CTC ticks per frame.
tests.expect: lesson.ctc-polled-clock: CTC3 ticks of 32 T. asm/exolon_hooks.asm:1040: 28 MHz / 256, one tick = 32 T of 3.5 MHz. docs/TECHNIQUES.md:636: rate = clk28 / (prescaler x constant). book ch 6 (report A-N): independent of CPU speed.
tests.needs: all four CPU speeds (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I12: v = CTC3 ticks per frame at 3.5 MHz (prescaler 256, 8-frame average) (ticks); s7 / s14 / s28 = the same at 7, 14 and 28 MHz. PASS if the four 8-frame totals are within 8 ticks of each other (1 tick per frame), else INFO.

tests.title: CTC time constant
tests.purpose: What period does a CTC timer have for a given time constant (16 x tc with 0 = 256, or 16 x (1 + tc))? And does a CTC channel set its status bit with its interrupt off?
tests.method: 28 MHz, interrupts off. CTC0 as a timer, prescaler 16, interrupt disabled ($C5 = 0), time constant 109, then 219, then 0. For 50 frames NextReg $C9 bit 0 (CTC0 status) is polled and cleared by writing 1 each time it is seen; the sightings are counted. The ratio count(219) x 10000 / count(0) separates the formulas: 11690 for 16 x tc, 11682 for 16 x (1 + tc). Results in counts. The ULA-off part of the claim is not measured here.
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:634: rate = clk28 / (prescaler x time constant), constant 0 = 256 (RustyPixelsUK); Next Point's comment writes (1 + time constant); the two are ~1 % apart, not checked. book ch 4 (report A-N): CTC channels set their status bits even with their interrupt disabled; the ULA and line interrupt raise nothing when switched off.
tests.needs: 28 MHz (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I13: v = $C9 bit 0 sightings with time constant 109 over 50 frames (count); c219 = with 219; c256 = with 0 (256); r = c219 x 10000 / c256; choice = 16xtc if r >= 11686, else 16x1+tc. PASS (status bit works while polled) if v > 0, else INFO.

tests.title: interrupt ack cost
tests.purpose: How many T does it cost to accept a hardware-IM2 interrupt (acknowledge plus the handler's RETI), at 3.5 and at 28 MHz?
tests.method: Hardware IM2, ULA enabled, every vector points to a bare RETI. At line 150, 64 times: clear status, raise the ULA request with NEXTREG $20,$40, read CTC3 (prescaler 16, free running), EI, NOP, (handler), read CTC3, DI. The same 64 times without the $20 write; the difference per repeat is the acknowledge + RETI. At NextReg $07 = 0 and 3. Result in T at 3.5 MHz and clocks at 28 MHz. IM 1 is not measured (it needs the ROM handler).
tests.expect: book ch 2 (report D-N28, L2100): accepting an interrupt costs 19 T in IM 2 on 3.03 at every speed (21 T on 3.02 at 28 MHz), 13 T in IM 1, NMI 11 T. book ch 4 (report A, latency): the same source. The spec adds the handler's RETI (14 T) to the measured difference.
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode; 3.5 and 28 MHz (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I14: v = extra T per repeat at 3.5 MHz with the interrupt against without (acknowledge + RETI) (T); c28 = the same in clocks at 28 MHz; s1 / s0 = sums of the 64 CTC3 differences (ticks) with and without the request, from the last speed run (28 MHz); im1 = skipped-needs-rom. Always INFO.

tests.title: LD A,I P/V
tests.purpose: Does LD A,I report P/V = 0 when an interrupt is accepted during it (the NMOS Z80 quirk), even though interrupts are enabled?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode IM 2 with a counting handler, interrupts on. A tight loop runs LD A,I then JP PO (taken when P/V = 0) until the handler has counted 500 frames (with a loop guard). Each P/V = 0 is counted. Result in count.
tests.expect: docs/BRIEFING.md:123 and docs/LEARNINGS.md:14: the NMOS quirk applies (P/V reads 0 if an interrupt is accepted during LD A,I; JNext too), so read I twice. book ch 2 (report D-N25): LD A,I / LD A,R P/V is correct on the Next. The claim: 0 = no bug, more than 0 = bug present.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I15: v = times LD A,I gave P/V = 0 with interrupts on (count); runs = handler runs during the loop (about 500). Always INFO (0 = no quirk, more = the quirk is present).

tests.title: line int shares /INT
tests.purpose: In pulse mode, does an enabled line interrupt raise the same /INT as the frame interrupt, so a game's handler runs twice per frame?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode IM 2 counting handler, ULA interrupt and line interrupt at line 100 both on ($22 bit 1, $23 = 100, $C4 = 3). Count handler runs over 50 frames. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:372: the line interrupt raises the same /INT in pulse mode, so the game's handler runs a second time per frame; never enable it under a game. book ch 4 (report A): agrees. Both: 100 runs in 50 frames.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I16: v = handler runs over 50 frames with the ULA and line-100 interrupts on (count). PASS if 99-101, else FAIL.

tests.title: ULA enable $22 / $C4
tests.purpose: Is the ULA interrupt enable one switch shared by NextReg $22 bit 2 (1 = off) and $C4 bit 0 (1 = on), so the last write wins?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode IM 2 counting handler. Case a: write $22 bit 2 = 1 (off), then $C4 bit 0 = 1 (on); count runs over 5 frames and read $22 and $C4 back. Case b: clear $22 bit 2, write $C4 bit 0 = 1, then $22 bit 2 = 1; count over 5 frames and read both back. Port $FF is not written. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-N): one flip-flop shared by $22 bit 2 and $C4 bit 0 (also port $FF bit 6), the last write wins; the line enable is shared by $22 bit 1 and $C4 bit 1. docs/BRIEFING.md:374: names $22 bit 2 / $C4 bit 0 as the ULA-interrupt-off state a stub must not leave; no prediction about sharing.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I17: v = runs over 5 frames in case a ($22 off then $C4 on) (count); b = runs in case b ($C4 on then $22 off); nr22a / nrc4a = $22 and $C4 read back after case a; nr22b / nrc4b = after case b. PASS if v is 4-6 and b = 0 (last write wins), else FAIL.

tests.title: HW IM2 priority
tests.purpose: With hardware IM2 enabled but the CPU still in IM 1, do non-ULA requests wait, and then all fire in priority order once IM 2 is selected?
tests.method: 28 MHz. $C0 bit 0 = 1 (vector bits 7:5 = 000), CPU in IM 1 with interrupts off, line ($C4 bit 1) and CTC0 ($C5 bit 0) enabled, CTC0 not counting. At line 150, NEXTREG $20,$81 requests line + CTC0 in software. Then IM 2 (I = $FC, 16 indexed handlers at $FC00), EI, a short loop, DI. The handlers log the vector offsets in the order they ran; $C8 and $C9 are read after. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-N): in IM 1 only the ULA interrupt falls back to a pulse; other sources wait and all fire, in priority order, when IM 2 is executed. The spec reads this as: line ($00) first, then CTC0 ($06).
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I18: v = handler runs after IM 2 + EI (count); o1 / o2 / o3 = vector offsets in the order the handlers ran ($hh; $FF = no run; line = $00, CTC0 = $06 with bits 7:5 = 000); c8 / c9 = NextRegs $C8 and $C9 after. Always INFO.

tests.title: RETI / RETN rules
tests.purpose: In hardware IM2 mode, does only RETI release the in-service source (RETN releases nothing), and do $C0 bits 2:1 read back the CPU's interrupt mode?
tests.method: 28 MHz, hardware IM2, ULA source only; the handler counts and ends with EI ; RETN. Interrupts on for 5 frames (raster polling). Then, under DI, $C0 is read in IM 1 and in IM 2. Recovery: pulse mode and a dummy RETI with interrupts off. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-N): only RETI (ED 4D) releases the in-service source and only in IM 2; RETN releases nothing; $C0 bits 2:1 read back the mode. docs/TECHNIQUES.md:606: a handler ending plain RET leaves the interrupt unacknowledged and no later interrupt arrives until a RETI runs. Expected: 1 run in 5 frames.
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode (set by the test)
tests.hazard: Could hang: the RETN handler leaves the interrupt unacknowledged; a dummy RETI recovers. The progress record is marked first: if the machine stops, the next start resumes and marks the test HANG-GUARD. Interrupt state is restored after.
tests.fields: I19: v = handler runs over 5 frames with a RETN-ended handler (count); im1 = $C0 read in IM 1 ($hh); im2 = $C0 read in IM 2. PASS if v = 1 and $C0 bits 2:1 read 01 in IM 1 and 10 in IM 2, else INFO.

tests.title: one outstanding CTC
tests.purpose: Does an interrupt source keep only one outstanding request, so CTC ticks that arrive while it waits fold into one?
tests.method: 28 MHz. CTC0 timer, prescaler 16, constant 175 (~10 kHz). Periods per frame counted by polling $C9 bit 0. Then hardware IM2, CTC0 only: (old part) a handler busy for 3 CTC0 periods counts its runs over one frame. Deciding part, 8 times: interrupts off for 5 CTC0 wraps (5 requests), EI just after the 5th wrap, DI half a period later; a handler that only counts. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-N): a source has one outstanding request; ticks arriving while it is pending or in service fold into it, only the status bit records them. So 1 run per window.
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: v = the most handler runs in one interrupts-on window after 5 CTC0 wraps with interrupts off (1 = the requests folded into one, 2-5 = they queued); least = the fewest; runs / periods = the old busy-handler ratio (board runs 4 / 5: 0.24-0.25), which cannot decide fold against queue.

tests.title: NR $20 generate
tests.purpose: Does writing NextReg $20 raise an interrupt request in software, whatever the source's enable, in pulse mode and in hardware IM2 mode?
tests.method: 28 MHz. At line 150 with interrupts on: NEXTREG $20,$40 (ULA request), four NOPs, DI; count handler runs and read $C8. Four cases: pulse mode IM 2 with the ULA enable ($C4 bit 0) on and off, hardware IM2 (I = $FC, every vector to the counter) with the enable on and off. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: book ch 4 (report A-N): NextReg $20 raises a request in software (bit 7 line, bit 6 ULA, bits 3:0 CTC) whatever the enables, in either mode.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I21: v = handler runs in pulse mode with the ULA enable on (count); poff = pulse mode, enable off; hon / hoff = hardware IM2 with the enable on / off; c8pon / c8poff / c8hon / c8hoff = NextReg $C8 after each case ($hh). Always INFO.

tests.title: DMA loses pulse
tests.purpose: Does a continuous zxnDMA transfer that covers the pulse-mode frame interrupt make the CPU lose that interrupt?
tests.method: Pulse mode IM 2 counting handler, interrupts on. A continuous 16K memory-to-memory DMA copy (bank 5 $4000 into suite pages mapped at $0000) is started 20 lines before the measured ULA interrupt line at 3.5 MHz, and 5 lines before at 28 MHz. Runs are counted from the start to the end of the transfer; $C8 is read after and the copy checked. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:250: the CPU cannot see a pulse-mode interrupt while the DMA owns the bus, so a transfer across it loses the frame interrupt (DI does not help). lesson.dma-copy-loses-interrupt: a DMA job holds the bus and can hide the frame interrupt. book ch 5 (report B-N19): lost in pulse mode (a 16K copy at 6 T/byte costs one).
tests.needs: 3.5 and 28 MHz (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I22: v = handler runs during the 16K transfer at 3.5 MHz (count); r28 = the same at 28 MHz; c8 / c8_28 = NextReg $C8 after each ($hh); bad / bad28 = copied bytes that are wrong. PASS if no run at either speed (the pulse was lost), else INFO.

tests.title: burst DMA + interrupt
tests.purpose: Does a burst-mode DMA with a prescaler hand the bus back between bytes, so a pulse-mode interrupt is still seen during a slow transfer?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pulse mode IM 2 counting handler, interrupts on. Burst-mode DMA, prescaler 100, 2K copy from $4000 to suite memory at $0000, started at line 150. The CPU waits (up to 40 frames) until the last byte is copied, counting handler runs meanwhile; the copy is checked. Result in runs (count).
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:256: burst mode + prescaler hands the bus back to the CPU between bytes, so the pulse interrupt is seen (hardware to confirm). book ch 5 (report B-N15): the CPU keeps more than 95 % at P = 100.
tests.needs: 28 MHz (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: I23: v = handler runs during the burst transfer (count); frames = frames waited until the last byte was copied (40 = did not finish); bad = copied bytes that are wrong. PASS if v > 0 and the transfer finished within 40 frames, else INFO.

tests.title: DMA yields to HW IM2
tests.purpose: In hardware IM2 mode with the DMA interrupt enables ($CC-$CE) set, does a running DMA let an enabled interrupt in and then resume after RETI? And what happens with interrupts off?
tests.method: 28 MHz, hardware IM2, ULA source, $CC = $01, interrupts on: continuous 16K copy ($4000 to suite memory at $0000, destination pre-filled with the inverse) started 5 lines before the ULA line. The handler records the raster line and how many bytes were copied (binary search of the destination). 3 frames are waited, then the copy is checked. Then the same transfer with interrupts off. Any request already waiting is taken first. Result in bytes.
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:259: hardware IM2 mode ($C0 bit 0 + $CC-$CE) can let interrupts break into a DMA. docs/DDMA.md:35: with hardware IM2 and enabled pending sources, the DMA may wait indefinitely under DI. book ch 4/5 (report A-C3, B-N19): the DMA releases the bus per byte while a source requests; the transfer resumes after RETI.
tests.needs: hardware IM2 mode (set by the test)
tests.hazard: Could hang: with interrupts off the DMA may wait for an acknowledge that never comes. The progress record is marked first: if the machine stops, the next start resumes and marks the test HANG-GUARD. Interrupt state is restored after.
tests.fields: v = bytes the DMA had copied when the handler ran; line = where; bad = wrong bytes after the EI run; dbad = wrong bytes after the interrupts-off run; pend = requests already waiting before the start (taken first); di = completes / returned-not-copied / paused-at-request. Board run 5: 1212 bytes at line 248, bad=0; dbad=15203 = 1181 bytes copied: with interrupts off the DMA stops at the ULA request at the same place and, with no acknowledge, does not restart - the CPU runs on (no hang).

tests.title: lines per frame
tests.purpose: How many raster lines does a 50 Hz frame have at the video timing in use?
tests.method: At the start speed, read the raster line ($1F, $1E, $1F: LSB, MSB, LSB, retried if the second LSB is lower) in a tight loop for 10 frames and keep the largest value; lines per frame = largest + 1. The expected value comes from the timing: HDMI ($11 bits 2:0 = 7) 312; otherwise $03 bits 6:4: 48K 312, 128K / +3 311, Pentagon 320. Other timings are in the opt-in TIMING group. Result in lines.
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:281: 48K 312 lines, 128K 311, Pentagon 320 on VGA; HDMI 312 whatever the machine timing. book ch 10 (report A, AGREES): 312 / 311 / 320.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: F01: v = lines per frame, the largest raster line over 10 frames + 1 (0 = no wrap seen) (lines); exp = the expected count for the timing in use (0 = no reference); nr03 = NextReg $03 ($hh). PASS if v = exp, else INFO.

tests.title: line length
tests.purpose: How long is one raster line, in T of 3.5 MHz?
tests.method: At 28 MHz, CTC3 runs free with prescaler 16 (one tick = 16 clocks of 28 MHz = 2 T of 3.5 MHz). The ticks are counted (wraps tracked by polling) over 256 line changes of the raster LSB ($1F). T per line = ticks x 2 / 256. Measured at the refresh rate in use. Result in T (2 decimals).
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:282: 896 clocks of 28 MHz a line (48K, Pentagon) = 224 T, 912 (128K) = 228 T, 864 (HDMI 50 Hz), 858 (HDMI 60 Hz). docs/LEARNINGS.md:33: 224 T (48K), 228 T (128K). book ch 10 (report A-N): 456 dots a line at 128K.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: F02: v = line length in T of 3.5 MHz (CTC3 ticks x 2 / 256 lines) (T); ticks256 = raw CTC3 ticks (prescaler 16) over the 256 lines. Always INFO.

tests.title: 60 Hz frame
tests.purpose: How many lines does a frame have at the other refresh rate (60 Hz, or 50 Hz if the machine started at 60), and when does a write to NextReg $05 bit 2 take effect?
tests.method: Read $05; at line 100 flip bit 2 (read-modify-write). The frames are then measured by the line number falling: f1 from line 100 of the switch frame to its wrap, f2-f4 the next three; $05 is read once after them. Then lines per frame over 10 frames and the line length (CTC3, as F02) at the new rate. Bit 2 is put back the same way and two frames waited. Results in lines.
tests.expect: lesson.frame-lines-at-60hz-unsettled: open; book 264, docs 262 / 261. docs/TECHNIQUES.md:282: 60 Hz 262 (48K, HDMI) / 261 (128K VGA). docs/TECHNIQUES.md:425: zxnext-copper-samples notes give 264 at 60 Hz. book ch 10 (report A-C1): 264, display from line 40. docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:32: the new rate takes effect at the next frame, $05 reads the old rate until then; book silent on the read-back.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: The refresh rate is switched twice (to the other rate and back), so the monitor may lose the picture for a moment. The start rate is always put back, even if a measurement fails.
tests.fields: F03: v = lines per frame at the other rate, largest line over 10 frames + 1 (lines); to = the rate switched to (60 or 50); nr05 = NextReg $05 read after 4 frames at the new rate ($hh); f1 = lines from line 100 of the switch frame to its wrap (+1); f2 / f3 / f4 = frame lengths of the next three frames; j2 = the line read just after f2's wrap; line_t = line length at the new rate (T of 3.5 MHz). Always INFO (the intake decides). Note: $05 is read once, not every line as the spec planned.

tests.title: raster read monotonic
tests.purpose: Does reading the raster line as LSB, MSB, LSB (retrying when the second LSB is lower) always give a correct, steadily rising value?
tests.method: 100,000 reads at 3.5 MHz and 100,000 at 28 MHz, in a tight loop, each by the house method ($1F, $1E, $1F with a retry if the second LSB is lower). A read is bad if it is above the largest line of the frame (measured at start-up) or lower than the one before other than at the frame wrap (from within 4 of the last line to within 4 of 0). Result in bad reads (count). The pair-until-agree lag in the spec is not measured.
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:332: a board with core 3.01.00 at 3.5 MHz sometimes read a wrong $1F; crossing line 255 -> 256 between the $1E and $1F reads gives a value 256 lines off; read LSB, MSB, LSB for timing; a pair read until two agree returns a late line (0-3 lines late at 3.5 MHz, docs/LEARNINGS.md). book ch 10 (report A-N): read $1E, $1F, $1E.
tests.needs: 3.5 and 28 MHz (set by the test)
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: F04: v = bad raster reads at both speeds together (count); bad35 = bad reads at 3.5 MHz; bad28 = at 28 MHz; maxline = the largest line of the frame used as the limit. PASS if v = 0, else FAIL.

tests.title: $64 line offset
tests.purpose: Does NextReg $64 offset the raster counter, the line interrupt and the copper alike, and when does a new value take effect?
tests.method: At line 100 write $64 = 32 and read the line straight after; measure the length of that frame and the next by the line number falling; put $64 back. Then with $64 = 0 and = 32: the raster line read in a line-interrupt-32 handler (pulse IM 2, ULA off), and the line at which the CPU first sees a copper WAIT 32 + MOVE $7F,$5A take effect (28 MHz). $64 restored and two frames waited. Results in lines.
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:279: $64 offsets $1E/$1F, the line interrupt and the copper WAIT alike. docs/TECHNIQUES.md:293: with 32, line 32 = ULA row 0; a new value takes effect when the ULA reaches row 0 (up to a frame late). docs/BRIEFING.md:383: a developer's note and the register text say 32 (demos use 33 for the Layer 2 top). book ch 10 (report A, AGREES): 32.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (NextReg $64 is put back to its start value and two frames waited, before any later raster wait)
tests.fields: F05: v = the raster line read straight after writing $64 = 32 at line 100 (lines); before = 100 (the line of the write); f1 = length of that frame (largest line + 1); f2 = length of the next frame; li0 / li32 = the line read in a line-interrupt-32 handler with $64 = 0 / 32 (65535 = never ran); cp0 / cp32 = the line where the copper WAIT 32 + MOVE was first seen with $64 = 0 / 32 (65535 = never); parts = raster,line-int,copper. Always INFO.

tests.title: 50 / 60 Hz table
tests.purpose: Side-by-side frame numbers at 50 and 60 Hz; for the claim: at 60 Hz, how many lines before the display does the frame interrupt come?
tests.method: At the start rate and then the other ($05 bit 2, read-modify-write, put back after even if a number is missing, two frames waited): lines per frame over 4 frames; line length (CTC3 prescaler 16 over 256 lines at 28 MHz, T of 3.5 MHz); and the raster line at which $C8 bit 0 (ULA interrupt status) is first seen set, polled at 28 MHz with interrupts off. Results in lines.
tests.expect: lesson.frame-lines-at-60hz-unsettled: the 60 Hz frame is open; the book gives 264 lines with the display from line 40, docs/TECHNIQUES.md 262 / 261. book ch 10 (report A-N): at 60 Hz the frame interrupt comes only 40 lines before the display, and there is no border above / below the wide area.
tests.needs: nothing special (a warning line is shown on screen)
tests.hazard: The test entry lists none, but it switches the refresh rate (to the other rate and back), so the picture may blink; the screen says to reset and restart if no picture returns within 10 s. The start rate is always put back.
tests.fields: The same numbers at both rates ($05 bit 2 switched and put back): l50 / l60 lines per frame, t50 / t60 line length in T (3.5 MHz), i50 / i60 the raster line at which the ULA interrupt status ($C8 bit 0) was first seen. v = l60. The intake prints them side by side.

tests.title: WAIT for a passed line
tests.purpose: Does a copper WAIT for a raster line the beam has already passed this frame hold the rest of the list until that line comes round in the next frame?
tests.method: 28 MHz ($07 = 3). List (uploaded by NextReg $60 after $61 / $62 = 0): MOVE $7F,1; WAIT line 150; MOVE $7F,2; WAIT line 50; MOVE $7F,3; HALT, started in mode 01 ($62 = $40) at raster line 10. The CPU polls NextReg $7F and the $1E / $1F raster line in one loop for up to 3 frames and logs, for values 1-3, the frame of the first sighting and the raster lines read just before and just after that $7F read. The result is a choice word.
tests.expect: lesson.copper-wait-line-equality (wiki copper page: WAIT is an equality match), docs/TECHNIQUES.md:203 and docs/BRIEFING.md:383: a WAIT for a line already passed holds the rest of the list until the next frame (the repo marks this as inferred from the guide, not tested); so 3 should appear at line 50 of the frame after the one where 2 appeared.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back)

tests.purpose: Does a copper WAIT for a horizontal position already passed on the current line go straight on (a >= compare), rather than wait for the next frame?

tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back)

tests.title: copper line vs raster

One loop reads CTC3, then $1F, then $7F, keeping the CTC value at the first sight of line L and of $7F = $AA, then reads the line. Each L runs in 3 frames; offset in T (3.5 MHz) = ticks x 2, median and spread reported. PASS if every line read equals L.

The claim (wiki copper page) adds that the horizontal count starts 12 dots before the display, so the copper counts the left border of line n+1 as line n. Claim tolerance: line exact, offset +-8 T. docs/LEARNINGS.md:596 is also cited; the text at that line is not about the copper.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back)

Board runs 4 and 5: o191 = -62 / -60 with s191 = 0 and 0 at lines 0, 120, 250: a WAIT for line 191 - the last display line - takes effect about 60 T (a quarter line) before the counter reads 191, every frame; the other lines coincide within the poll step. The copper line number still equals the counter (l191 = 191).

tests.title: copper instruction time
tests.purpose: How many 28 MHz clocks does the copper take per MOVE and per WAIT instruction?
tests.method: 28 MHz, CTC3 /16 (a tick = 16 clocks of 28 MHz). List: WAIT (100, 0); MOVE $7F,1; 1000 x MOVE $7F,1; MOVE $7F,$AA; HALT, started at line 90. The CPU polls $7F and counts CTC3 ticks (wraps counted) from its first sight of 1 to its first sight of $AA = 1001 instructions. Again with 1000 x WAIT (100, 0) (already matched) in place of the 1000 MOVEs. Clocks per instruction = ticks x 16 / 1001.
tests.expect: lesson.copper-clock-and-instruction-time (wiki copper page: MOVE 2, WAIT 1): the copper runs at 28 MHz; a MOVE takes 2 copper clocks and a WAIT 1; the register holds the new value 2 clocks after the MOVE. Claim tolerance +-0.1 clock.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back)
tests.fields: P05: v = 28 MHz clocks per MOVE, 2 decimals (clocks; -1 when 1 or $AA was never seen); wait = the same per already-matched WAIT; mt / wt = the raw CTC3 tick counts (16 clocks each) of the MOVE run and the WAIT run, 65535 = timed out. INFO always.

tests.title: copper restart line
tests.purpose: In copper mode 11 (restart every frame), at which raster line does the list start again?
tests.method: 28 MHz. Mode 11 ($62 = $C0) list: MOVE $7F,9; WAIT line 200; MOVE $7F,1; HALT. At raster line 210 the CPU writes $7F = 0, then polls $7F (up to 65536 reads) and reads the $1E / $1F raster line when 9 appears again, i.e. when the list has restarted. Result in lines.
tests.expect: lesson.copper-wait-offsets and docs/TECHNIQUES.md:423 (raster counters and the top border: the border lines above ULA line 0 count as the end of the previous frame): the claim says mode 11 restarts every frame at line 0 of the copper count, after the top border, not at the frame's first line; the claim records CSpect restarting after the top border.
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back)
tests.fields: P06: v = the raster line at which $7F = 9 was first seen after it was cleared at line 210 (lines); $FF (hex) when 9 never came back within the poll limit. INFO always.

tests.title: MOVE $44 pair
tests.purpose: Do two copper MOVEs to NextReg $44 write one 9-bit palette entry, as two CPU writes to $44 do?
tests.method: CPU speed as found (not set). Layer 2 first palette entry 200 saved ($43 = $10, $40 = 200, read $41 and $44). List: MOVE $43,$10; MOVE $40,200; MOVE $44,$A5; MOVE $44,$01; HALT, run in mode 01 for a 256-pass DJNZ delay, then stopped. The CPU selects entry 200 again and reads $41 (8-bit value) and $44 (9th-bit byte). Entry 200, $43 and $40 are put back.

tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back); palette entry 200 restored
tests.fields: P07: v = NextReg $41 read for Layer 2 palette entry 200 after the copper ran (hex); b9 = NextReg $44 read for that entry (the 9th-bit byte, hex). PASS if v = $A5, else FAIL.

tests.title: copper + CPU coexist
tests.purpose: Can the CPU write and read palette entries by NextReg while the copper loops MOVEs to another register, and what happens when the copper writes the palette index the CPU uses?

The copper loops 1024 x MOVE $7F,$55 (APART) or 1024 x MOVE $40,0 (SHARE) in mode 01 while the CPU selects sprite palette 2 ($43 = %01100000), writes 256 entries by NEXTREG $41 (value i xor $5A), then reads each back ($40 = i, $41 through $243B / $253B) and counts wrong entries (shown up to 255). tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back); sprite palette 2 saved and written back

PASS if a35 = 0 and a28 = 0, else FAIL; s35 / s28 are information only (wrong entries expected).

tests.title: NEXTREG collision
tests.purpose: When the CPU writes a NextReg while the copper is writing NextRegs, does the CPU wait, and how much does each NEXTREG cost?
tests.method: 28 MHz, CTC3 /256 (a tick = 256 clocks of 28 MHz). 2048 x NEXTREG $7F,0 (8 per DJNZ pass) timed three ways: copper stopped; copper looping 1024 x MOVE $7F,$55 (same register); copper looping MOVE $40,0 (another register; $40 put back). Clocks per NEXTREG = ticks x 256 / 2048, the DJNZ share (13 / 8 a NEXTREG) included. Raster lines elapsed are kept as a cross-check against a CTC wrap.

tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back)
tests.fields: P09: v = 28 MHz clocks per NEXTREG with the copper stopped, 2 decimals (clocks); mv = the same with the copper looping MOVE $7F; mp = with it looping MOVE $40; t0 / t1 / t2 = raw CTC3 ticks (256 clocks each) of the three runs; l0 / l1 / l2 = raster lines elapsed in each run (a wrap past 256 ticks would show as a small t with many lines). INFO always.

tests.title: same mode no restart
tests.purpose: Does rewriting $61 / $62 with the same copper mode (11) only move the index, without restarting a running list?
tests.method: 28 MHz. Mode 11 list: MOVE $7F,9; WAIT line 150; MOVE $7F,2; HALT, running. At raster line 100 the CPU writes $7F = 0, then $61 = 0 and $62 = $C0 (mode 11 again, index 0) and reads $7F at line 110 of the same frame. A restart would have run MOVE $7F,9 again.

tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (the harness stops the copper afterwards and puts NextRegs $7F and $43 back)
tests.fields: P10: v = NextReg $7F read at line 110 (hex): 0 = no restart, 9 = the list restarted. PASS if 0, else FAIL.

tests.title: DMA correct
tests.purpose: Does the zxnDMA copy and fill memory correctly at 3.5 MHz as well as at 28 MHz?
tests.method: Scratch pages 38 / 39 in slots 0 / 1, interrupts off; port $6B, nextbench program shape: $C3, then $83; WR0 $7D + A address + length; WR1 / WR2 (bit 6 + timing byte 2); WR4 $AD (continuous) + B address; $82; $CF; $87. At 3.5 MHz ($07 = 0) and 28 MHz ($07 = 3): a 2048-byte copy $0000 -> $2000 (destination first set to NOT the source) and a 256-byte fill from one fixed source byte $55 (WR1 $24) into $2000. Every byte checked.
