tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: D01: v = how many of the four transfers had wrong bytes (0-4); c35 / f35 = wrong bytes of the 2K copy / the 256-byte fill at 3.5 MHz; c28 / f28 = the same at 28 MHz. PASS if all four are 0, else FAIL.

tests.title: DMA cost per byte
tests.purpose: How many 28 MHz clocks does a zxnDMA byte cost, memory to memory and memory to port, with no timing byte and with each timing byte, and does 'no timing byte' mean 3-clock cycles?
tests.method: Pages 38 / 39 in slots 0 / 1. Continuous transfers on $6B from $0000 to $2000 (memory) or to port $5B (sprite patterns from slot 63; WR2 $28 = fixed I/O), timing byte absent or WR1 and WR2 bit 6 + byte %01 / %10 / %11, 256 and 2048 bytes, at 3.5 and 28 MHz. The CPU is frozen during the transfer, so the time is rebuilt from the raster line, CTC0 (/256) and CTC3 (/16) read before and after. 28 MHz clocks per byte = (t2048 - t256) / 1792.
tests.expect: docs/DDMA.md:62 / :88 (3.03.00 guide): after $C3 3 + 3 cycles = 6 a byte; fastest 2 + 2 = 4, about 12 % faster. docs/TECHNIQUES.md:232-233: ~4 cycles a byte at length 2 only with the timing byte sent for both ports; without it standard Z80 cycle timing. book ch 5 (B-N1, N2, N31, B-C1): 6 / 4 clocks, 7 at 28 MHz on 3.02; 3-clock cycles after reset; timing byte 00 = 4, 01 = 3, 10 = 2, 11 = 4 clocks a cycle (as quoted in g6.asm).
tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (it writes sprite pattern memory from pattern 63 on; not restored, nothing displays it)
tests.fields: keys <m|p><a|3|4|2><35|28> = clocks of 28 MHz per byte (memory / port $5B; timing byte absent / 3 / 4 / 2; 3.5 / 28 MHz), slope (t2048 - t256) / 1792. Board run 5 (d99fbf8): 0 / 584 / 0.32 were a timing fault - in continuous mode the CPU is frozen and the CTC3 wraps were lost; the board's own nb.DMA rows predict about 4.99 clocks (28 MHz) and 32 (3.5 MHz) at timing byte 2. method=fault marks a slope outside 0.5-100 (INFO, never FAIL). PASS if absent = timing byte 3 within 0.10 at 28 MHz and 0.80 at 3.5 MHz (values 8 times larger there; one timing step is 0.16).

tests.title: DMA length rule
tests.purpose: How many bytes does a DMA transfer of programmed length 0, 1 and 16 move on port $6B (zxnDMA) and on port $0B (Zilog mode)?
tests.method: Pages 38 / 39 in slots 0 / 1, CPU speed as found. Source $0000 = 1, 2, 3, ...; destination $2000 = 32 bytes of $AA. Programs of length 0, 1 and 16 (timing byte 2, continuous) are sent and started through $6B, then the same through $0B; after each transfer $C3 is written to $6B and $6B is read (zxnDMA mode back). Bytes no longer $AA are counted.

tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none (zxnDMA mode is restored by a $6B access after each $0B pass)

tests.title: DMA prescaler
tests.purpose: With prescaler P in burst mode, how many 28 MHz clocks pass per DMA byte at 3.5 and at 28 MHz?
tests.method: Pages 38 / 39 in slots 0 / 1. Burst mode (WR4 $CD), 256 bytes $0000 -> $2000, WR2 timing byte 2 with bit 5 + prescaler byte P, for P = 0, 1, 12, 55, 100, 144 at 3.5 and 28 MHz. The CPU polls the last destination byte (first set to NOT the source) for the end while counting CTC3 /16 ticks (wraps counted). 28 MHz clocks per byte = ticks x 16 / 256; -1 when it timed out.

tests.hazard: none

tests.title: burst CPU share
tests.purpose: How much of the bus does the CPU keep during a burst-mode DMA with prescaler 100, and during a continuous one with the same prescaler?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pages 38 / 39. A 2048-byte $0000 -> $2000 transfer with prescaler 100 (timing byte 2), once burst (WR4 $CD) and once continuous ($AD), while the CPU runs a polling loop (reads CTC3 /16, waits for the last destination byte). The same loop then runs with no DMA for about as many CTC wraps. Share (%) = loop passes per 16 ticks with the DMA / passes per 16 ticks without x 100.

tests.needs: nothing special
tests.hazard: none
tests.fields: v = the CPU's polling-loop rate during a burst (P = 100) against the same loop with no DMA, %; cont = the same during a continuous transfer. Board run 5 (d99fbf8): 104 % came from comparing loop counts over different lengths; rates are compared now.

tests.title: DMA read status
tests.purpose: What does the DMA status byte read when the DMA is idle and after a finished block, and does the read sequence follow the read mask?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pages 38 / 39. $C3, then $BF (read status) and IN from $6B -> v. A 16-byte continuous copy is programmed and run, then $BF and IN -> s1. Then $BB with read mask $7F, $A7 (start the read sequence) and 7 reads from $6B -> r0-r6.

tests.hazard: none

tests.title: $C3 keeps program
tests.purpose: Does $C3 (reset) keep the programmed addresses and length, so that $CF, $87 alone repeats the same copy, and at what speed does it then run?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pages 38 / 39. A 64-byte continuous copy $0000 -> $2000 with timing byte 2 is programmed, run and timed. The destination is cleared, then only $C3, $CF (load) and $87 (enable) are written; the copy is checked and timed again (CTC3 /16 with raster / CTC0 rebuild, the CPU being frozen). 28 MHz clocks per byte = ticks x 16 / 64, timing-loop overhead included.

tests.hazard: none

tests.title: overlap fill
tests.purpose: Does a forward DMA copy with destination = source + 1 fill the block with the first byte, like the LDIR fill idiom?
tests.method: 28 MHz, pages 38 / 39. $0000 = $5A, $0001-$0100 = NOT of a pattern; a 256-byte continuous copy $0000 -> $0001 (timing byte 2). Bytes $0001-$0100 that are not $5A are counted. (The claim's measure names 3.5 and 28 MHz; the code runs at 28 MHz only.)

tests.title: blitter detect
tests.purpose: Is the zxnDDMA blitter present? Probe: on a DMA without it the extended command bytes are dropped and their data bytes act as ordinary register bytes.
tests.method: 28 MHz, pages 38 / 39 in slots 0 / 1; byte 0 of pages 56 / 57 saved, set to 0 / $22, written back after. To $6B: $C3; $D7,$0B; $DB,$0B; $DF,$01 (physical; every data byte below $80); eight $83; a 1-byte copy $2000 -> $0000 ($7D,$00,$20,$01,$00,$14,$10,$AD,$00,$00,$82,$CF,$87); $C3. A blitter copies physical $0B2000 (page 57 byte 0) to $0B0000 (page 56 byte 0); an old DMA copies $2000 (page 39, $11) to $0000 (page 38).

FAIL if v = none and the core is 3.03 or later (NextReg $01 >= $33); otherwise INFO.

tests.title: blitter physical
tests.purpose: Are blitter physical addresses SRAM addresses, with 8K RAM page n at $40000 + n x $2000, and does an address carry across a 64K boundary into the extended byte?
tests.method: 28 MHz. Physical mode ($DF bit 0), $D7 / $DB extended bytes $08, no timing byte. 16 bytes $08C100 -> $08E100 (page 38 +$100 to page 39 +$100), read through the MMU (slots 0 / 1), with 16 guard bytes before and 32 after checked still $AA. Cross: 16 bytes from $08FFF8 (the last 8 of page 39, then 8 more where the address carries) to page 38 +$200, compared with page 39 and page 40 through slot 1.

tests.title: blitter BRAM
tests.purpose: Can blitter physical-mode writes reach the block-RAM pages (bank 5 page $0A, page $0E), or do they land in an invisible SRAM twin, while page $0F is ordinary SRAM?
tests.method: 28 MHz. For pages $0A, $0E, $0F at physical $054000 / $05C000 / $05E000 (extended byte $05): the 16 bytes there saved by a physical copy (to page 38 +$300) and through the MMU (slot 1, to +$320); a 16-byte pattern copied there physically; read back through the MMU and by a physical copy (to +$360); then the saved bytes put back both ways. shows = the MMU read sees the pattern; twin = only the physical read-back does.

tests.title: blitter 2D
tests.purpose: Does blitter 2D mode move row length x rows bytes with strides measured from row start to row start, and does a row length or row count of 0 still move one byte?

tests.title: frame rate (stopwatch)

Frames are counted from the raster line; CTC channel 3 (prescaler 256, time constant 256, 28 MHz clock) times the same interval. The operator types the watch's seconds and tenths. Result: frames / seconds (Hz); NextRegs $05 and $11 read.
tests.expect: docs/TECHNIQUES.md:639: clk28 = 28.0-33 MHz for VGA timings 0-6 (27 MHz HDMI); a '50 Hz' frame is 50.00, 51.02, 52.61, 53.57, 55.36, 57.14, 58.93 Hz on VGA 0-6, 50.00 on HDMI. docs/BRIEFING.md:108: '50 Hz' is exact only at VGA 0 and HDMI; up to 58.93 Hz on VGA 1-6; not measured on a board.

tests.hazard: none (only the picture changes; the harness puts back the NextRegs, palette entries, clip windows and sprites it used)
tests.fields: V19: v = frames / watch seconds (Hz). cable = hdmi / vga / other; frames, secs, tenths (typed off the watch), tol (+-0.3 s as % of the time), r05 / r11. ctcw / c0 / c1: the same interval timed by CTC channel 3 (prescaler 256, time constant 256; the CTC clock is 28 MHz whatever the CPU speed, book ch 6): ticks = 256 x ctcw + c0 - c1, CTC time = ticks x 256 / 28,000,000 s. The intake gives the rate by both: a watch time unlike the CTC time is a timing error at the watch (or a 28 MHz clock that is off, which only the watch can show). Board run 8: 49.29 Hz +-0.19 by the watch (7592 frames / 154.0 s, HDMI; no CTC count in that build). The same file's F01 / F02 (311 lines of 228.02 T, T measured by the CTC as 8 clocks of 28 MHz) give 28,000,000 / (311 x 1824.2) = 49.36 Hz, inside the watch's range; 50.02 Hz is what the same 311 x 228 T give with the 128K's 3.5469 MHz clock instead.

tests.title: $BB bit 6
tests.purpose: Does NextReg $BB bit 6 = 1 enable or disable the DivMMC automap exit on an instruction fetch from $1FF8-$1FFF?
tests.method: Interrupts off. DivMMC is mapped by an RST 8 with a one-byte RET planted at the alt ROM's $0008 (delayed entry). With $BB as NextZXOS left it, a RET found in the DivMMC ROM at $1FF8-$1FFF is called ($C9 also planted at those alt ROM addresses): does the ROM come back? Then mapped again, $BB bit 6 flipped, the same RET: does DivMMC stay mapped? $BB put back, DivMMC unmapped and the ROM bytes checked.
tests.expect: docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md:35: $BB bit 6 = 1 DISABLES automap at $1FF8-$1FFF (official nextreg.txt); the varmfskii notes say it enables. book ch 3 (report D-C4): set = exit enabled. The launch value is evidence too: NextZXOS needs the exit.
tests.needs: opt-in group D (its hazard screen, Y); if it locks up: power off and on and start again (HANG-GUARD)
tests.hazard: maps DivMMC memory on purpose (alt ROM, NextReg $BB / $0A); could stop the machine or leave DivMMC mapped until reset (then a stop screen asks for a power cycle). Interrupts off throughout; never writes the SD card or port $E3; all changed registers and bytes are put back
tests.fields: Interrupts off throughout; nothing of NextZXOS runs. nrbb = $BB at the start. map = DivMMC mapped after an RST 8 with a one-byte RET at the alt ROM's $0008 (the entry is delayed: spec 1.1). dv = the 8 DivMMC ROM bytes at $1FF8-$1FFF. off = the RET found there (ra = its address; $C9 planted at all eight alt ROM addresses too) brought the ROM back with $BB as at launch. mapflip = DivMMC stayed mapped when the same RET ran with bit 6 flipped ($BB put back after). v = set-enables / set-disables (which value of bit 6 lets the exit run), no-change, no-entry (the RST 8 did not map DivMMC: nothing more tried), no-exit (no RET at $1FF8-$1FFF or it did not unmap: the flip not tried). INFO.

tests.title: $3Dxx instant automap
tests.purpose: With automap on and ROM 3 selected, does an instruction fetch at $3Dxx map DivMMC at once, so the code there comes from DivMMC and not the ROM image?
tests.method: Interrupts off. DivMMC mapped as in XD1; its RAM at $3D00-$3D01 saved and OR A : RET written there; unmapped by a RET at $1FF8-$1FFF. Alt ROM $3D00 = SCF : RET; $0A as at launch (automap on); CALL $3D00 with carry clear. Carry clear = DivMMC's code ran (instant); carry set = the alt ROM ran; DivMMC mapped afterwards is recorded. DivMMC bytes put back, DivMMC unmapped, ROM bytes checked.

Expected: instant.

tests.fields: Interrupts off throughout. DivMMC mapped as XD1; its RAM at $3D00-$3D01 saved and OR A : RET written there (ram = the write held); unmapped; alt ROM $3D00 = SCF : RET; CALL $3D00 with carry clear and $0A as at launch. Carry clear = DivMMC's OR A ran: the fetch at $3D00 came from DivMMC (instant, PASS); carry set and map = 1 = the alt ROM ran first and DivMMC mapped after (delayed, FAIL); neither = none (FAIL). The DivMMC bytes are put back. no-entry / no-exit / no-ram: the set-up was not possible (INFO, says why the rest is left out).

tests.title: auto-restart freeze
tests.purpose: Does a DMA transfer in continuous mode with auto-restart keep the bus forever, so the CPU never runs again unless an interrupt allowed to break in stops it?
tests.method: One DMA test byte first (a deaf DMA from an earlier XH2 gives SKIP). Hardware IM 2 (table at $FC00, ULA interrupt only), NextReg $CC bit 0 = 1 (ULA interrupt may break into a DMA transfer), EI. A 256-byte copy $0000 -> $2000, continuous, WR5 $A2 (auto-restart), $87. The main loop counts passes while the DMA runs; the handler counts interrupts and at the second sends $83 then $C3. Then DI, the copy checked. Result: passes (count).
tests.expect: book ch 5 (report B-N17): auto-restart in continuous mode never gives the CPU the bus back; only a reset or a yielding interrupt frees it. lesson.zxn-dma-autorestart-freeze: it froze the machine at once (observed on a board). Expected: few or no main-loop passes, the handler stops it.
tests.needs: opt-in group H (its hazard screen, Y); a working DMA (not left deaf by an earlier XH2); if the machine does not come back: reset and start again (HANG-GUARD)

tests.fields: v = main-loop passes between $87 and the stop (the CPU had the bus that often); irq = handler runs (the handler stops the DMA at the second); bad = bytes of the 256-byte copy that differ. PASS if stopped and v <= 50. A machine that does not come back = the escape (hardware IM2 + $CC) failed: HANG-GUARD. JNext 1.3.0 hangs here (no $CC escape); CSpect PASS v=1. The DMA must answer one byte first: a DMA still locked by an earlier XH2 gives SKIP why=dma-deaf (board run 7 pass 2 printed FAIL v=15812 bad=254 that way).

tests.title: WR4 interrupt lock
tests.purpose: Does a DMA WR4 byte with bit 4 set (interrupt control follows) leave the DMA deaf, and which reset (soft, hard, power cycle) frees it?
tests.method: One DMA test byte first (already deaf: SKIP). Else the progress record is marked, $91 (WR4 with bit 4) is sent to port $6B, and a 1-byte copy is tried: copied or not. The screen then asks to finish the group, reset or power-cycle and start the suite again. On that start one DMA byte is tried at once; XH2 then asks which reset was used (keys 1-3) and records whether the DMA answered.
tests.expect: book ch 5 (report B-N10): a WR4 byte with bit 4 leaves the DMA deaf until a machine reset; a hard or soft reset frees it. lesson.zxn-dma-wr4-interrupt-lock: byte $91 locked the DMA until power-off (one board, core 3.03.00; hard reset untested).
tests.needs: opt-in group H (its hazard screen, Y); a soft reset, hard reset or power cycle, then a restart of the suite and an operator answer (keys 1-3) for the follow-up
tests.hazard: leaves the DMA unusable on purpose until a reset (possibly until power-off); no other change. Run last in its group; the screen after it says what to do. Opt-in for that reason

Else before / after = 1-byte copies before and after the WR4 byte $91 (bit 4); v = deaf (PASS) or copied (FAIL). Then power off and on (or a hard reset), start again, H: a 1 / 2 / 3 question gives reset=soft / hard / power and v = reset-frees or still-locked (the start's DMA byte, PRG_XH2), OPERATOR. The verdict uses the lock pass; the note states each follow-up. Board run 7 (N-Go board, an Issue 2-compatible clone, core 3.03.00): pass 4 ran in the same run as the lock (no restart) and found the DMA still deaf; the files hold no start after a reset, so what F4 does is not yet shown.

claims.measure: Safe part (auto): record $BB as NextZXOS leaves it (NextZXOS needs the exit, so its value is evidence). OPT-IN part, interrupts off throughout: DivMMC mapped by an RST 8 with RET at the alt ROM's $0008; a RET at $1FF8-$1FFF called with $BB as at launch and again with bit 6 flipped; DivMMC still mapped after = that value stops the exit; $BB put back, DivMMC unmapped and the ROM bytes checked.
claims.risk: could leave DivMMC mapped until reset (then a stop screen, no file call); no SD write
